note: Liberia, read on 2026-10-30 in the Liberia Immigration Service's own Service Delivery Charter (dated 23 January 2025, on lis.gov.lr), whose service tables give each residence permit service with its cost, eligibility, requirements and time. The residence permit is one permit, not tied to a purpose (the LIS's mandate as the charter states it: 'Issue resident and other permits to persons desirous of residing in Liberia'), so it is written as a general route. Its cost depends on the holder's origin and the form holds one fee: the non-African's US$750 (service LIS-0001, the residence permit by change of status for a non-African) is written, in US dollars as the charter prices it; Africans pay another charge (ECOWAS citizens US$150, LIS-0007; other Africans their own rates, e.g. US$300 to renew), as do spouses and minor children (US$600 and US$400 for a non-African's). The charter gives 7 working days for processing, written as the time. A renewal is its own service (LIS-0001 of the renewals, US$350 for a non-African holding a valid permit), so the permit is renewable; the renewal's fee isn't held. The permit is granted as a change of status to a foreigner who 'must have passed through a legitimate border crossing point in Liberia' with an entry stamp, which suggests it is sought in the country, but the charter doesn't say where it is applied for in words, so that is left out. Neither the permit's term, the work it allows, nor any path to permanence is stated; those are left out.
